mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level relative to its 12-month moving average signals an easing monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.0% indicates a tightening monetary cycle, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market characterized by high employment growth (PAYEMS) and low unemployment (UNRATE) supports corporate earnings and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through joint effects.
failure_condition: The interaction term (PAYEMS growth * UNRATE) shows no significant positive correlation with 20-day SPX returns in a 3-year rolling window (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns due to reduced consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, a HOUST decline > 0.5% MoM does not lead to negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production (INDPRO) levels indicate robust economic activity and corporate output, supporting earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is above its 3-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL annualized growth above 3.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy and reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized growth > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales growth (RSAFS) combined with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a supportive consumer spending environment and low borrowing costs, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through interaction effects.
failure_condition: The interaction term (RSAFS growth * FEDFUNDS) shows no significant positive correlation with 20-day SPX returns in a 3-year rolling window (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market (UNRATE < 3.5%), a further decline in unemployment rate signals economic overheating and impending monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: In tight labor market periods (UNRATE < 3.5%), a UNRATE decline > 0.2pp does not lead to negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases.
